approach: The 1 kg block and the 2 kg block's movable pulley share one string, so the 1 kg block accelerates twice as fast; apply Newton's second law to each block.

steps.text: The string from the 1 kg block runs over the table-edge pulley, over the fixed ceiling pulley, under the movable pulley (carrying the 2 kg block), and ties off near the fixed pulley, so tension T2 is the same throughout this string and the movable pulley is held by two strands of T2.
steps.equation: same reasoning as the A-B movable-pulley constraint: a₁ = 2a, where a is the acceleration of the 2 kg and 3 kg blocks

steps.text: Write Newton's second law for the 1 kg block on the smooth table, pulled by T2 with acceleration a₁ = 2a.
Write Newton's second law for the 2 kg block (downward positive): weight down, T1 pulling it down toward the 3 kg block, two strands of T2 pulling it up.
Write Newton's second law for the 3 kg block (downward positive): weight down, T1 pulling it up.
The 2 kg and 3 kg blocks accelerate at 50/9 m/s² downward, the 1 kg block accelerates at 2 × 50/9 = 100/9 m/s² horizontally toward the pulley, T1 = 40/3 N ≈ 13.3 N and T2 = 100/9 N ≈ 11.1 N.

final_answer.value: (a) 1 kg block: 100/9 m/s² ≈ 11.1 m/s² (horizontal, toward the pulley); 2 kg and 3 kg blocks: 50/9 m/s² ≈ 5.6 m/s² (downward). (b) T1 = 40/3 N ≈ 13.3 N, T2 = 100/9 N ≈ 11.1 N.

common_mistakes.text: Missing the movable-pulley factor of 2 and writing a(1kg) = a(2kg), which gives the wrong tensions and accelerations.
Forgetting that the movable pulley is held up by two strands of T2 and writing the 2 kg equation with only one T2.
